results.title: DiViCo: Disentangled Visual Token Compression for Efficient Large Vision-Language Model
results.venue: IEEE transactions on circuits and systems for video technology (Print)
results.abstract: Large Vision-Language Models have drawn much attention and become increasingly applicable in complicated multimodal tasks such as visual question answering, video grounding, etc. However, it still suffers from inefficiency problem during the inference stage due to the computational overhead brought by the large number of visual tokens. Existing works either utilize an attention score (or visual-text relevance) to filter out the less significant visual tokens, or insert learnable projection layers to directly compress the tokens, which neglects the informative details in visual signals and introduces information loss, resulting in poor generalizability to test data. To solve these problems, in this paper we propose a novel Disentangled Visual Token Compression module, i.e., DiViCo, that effectively compresses the visual tokens and maintains good performance simultaneously. In concrete, we first select the top $\tau \%$ visual tokens according to their average attention scores, then predict the gap between these selected tokens and the original information by employing the chosen tokens in a disentangled and variational manner. Specifically, we model the mean and variance, sampling the predicted gap from the Gaussian prior. We further keep the informativeness of the compressed visual tokens via KL divergence, which ensures the generalizability of the model. Extensive experiments demonstrate the advantage of our proposed DiViCo module against several state-of-the-art baselines over various real-world datasets. Most notably, LLaVA-v1.5-7b equipped with DiViCo is able to reduce 67.7% FLOPs and save 51.7% time while maintaining 95.6% of the accuracy for LLaVA-v1.5-7b without any compression.

results.title: AVG-LLaVA: An Efficient Large Multimodal Model with Adaptive Visual Granularity
results.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
results.abstract: Recently, large multimodal models (LMMs) have achieved significant advancements. When dealing with high-resolution images, dominant LMMs typically divide them into multiple local images and a global image, leading to a large number of visual tokens. In this work, we introduce AVG-LLaVA, an LMM that can adaptively select the appropriate visual granularity based on the input image and instruction. Specifically, we first apply the multiple pooling layers to obtain visual tokens at different granularities. Then we propose a visual granularity router, which includes a Transformer layer, an MLP layer, and a voter layer, used to select the appropriate visual granularity based on the image and instruction. Furthermore, we put forward RGLF, a novel training paradigm that aims at aligning the granularity predicted by the router with the preferences of the LMM, without the need for additional manually annotated data. Extensive experiments and analysis show that AVG-LLaVA achieves superior performance across 11 benchmarks, as well as significantly reduces the number of visual tokens and speeds up inference (e.g., an 85.3% reduction in visual tokens and a 2.53$\times$ increase in inference speed on the AI2D benchmark).

results.title: Design of an FPGA-Based High-Throughput Matrix Multiplication Accelerator for Transformers
results.venue: International Conference on the Software Process
results.abstract: Matrix multiplication operations in large language models (LLMs) account for over 80% of the computational load in Transformer inference. Existing FPGA accelerators suffer from significant bottlenecks in on-chip memory access efficiency and pipeline throughput. This paper proposes a high-throughput matrix multiplication accelerator specifically designed for resource-constrained FPGAs. A hierarchical loop partitioning strategy eliminates memory port contention during block accesses; a refreshable pipeline mechanism substantially reduces loop boundary overhead; and a merged access pattern maximizes off-chip memory bandwidth utilization. Implemented on a Xilinx XCZU15EG FPGA and validated through RTL co-simulation, this design achieves 2.52x acceleration over an optimized baseline, with 85% DSP utilization and energy efficiency of 20.5 GOPs/W—delivering up to 15.9x higher performance than the NVIDIA V100S GPU.

results.title: Collaborative Edge Inference for Large Language Models with Speculative Decoding
results.venue: ICC 2026 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
results.abstract: Existing edge-based large language model (LLM) serving systems primarily rely on autoregressive decoding (AD) to generate inference results, generating only one output token per forward pass. The AD process underutilizes GPUs’ parallel processing capabilities and inherently introduces high serving latency, thereby hindering efficient LLM serving in resource-constrained edge networks. To address this challenge, we propose a speculative decoding (SD)-based LLM serving framework that coordinates small and large models deployed on heterogeneous edge nodes to accelerate output token generation and thus reduce serving latency. To improve resource utilization of edge nodes, we introduce pipeline parallelism that groups multiple inference tasks into batches and processes them in a pipelined manner. Building on this framework, we derive the total serving latency that jointly considers communication and inference latencies. We then formulate a joint task batching and wireless communication resource allocation problem to minimize the total serving latency under computing and communication resource constraints. To solve this problem, we derive closed-form solutions for wireless communication resource allocation, and develop an efficient algorithm to obtain optimal task batching strategies. Simulation results show that the proposed LLM serving framework outperforms benchmarks, achieving up to 23.1% latency reduction.

results.title: MESO: Memory-Efficient Speculative Offloading for Large Language Model Inference
results.venue: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network
results.abstract: In resource-constrained devices, Large Language Model (LLM) inference faces significant challenges due to limited GPU memory resources. Existing studies, such as SpecOffload, combine offloading with speculative decoding to utilize a draft model for generating candidate tokens, thereby improving LLM generation throughput. However, they require the draft model to reside permanently in GPU memory. In resource-constrained devices, it tends to introduce high fixed overheads, resulting in low memory efficiency, which can be measured by the throughput gain per unit of GPU memory usage. To address this limitation, we propose MESO, a framework that specializes in improving memory efficiency. Specifically, MESO achieves high memory efficiency by offloading the draft model, enabling fine-grained asynchronous component loading, and leveraging pinned memory optimization. Experimental results show that compared to the selected baselines, MESO achieves 1.35× memory efficiency on average across various scenarios, and delivers up to 2.25× memory efficiency. Additionally, MESO reduces peak GPU memory usage by more than 50% compared to SpecOffload. Quantitative and qualitative analyses further validate the effectiveness of MESO.

results.title: CoS-VQ: Coordinated Shared-Scale Vector Quantization for Large Language Models
results.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) require substantial memory, motivating low-bit weight quantization for efficient deployment. Existing vector quantization (VQ) methods often improve accuracy by increasing the effective coding dimension, which can complicate independent lookup and local codeword updates. We propose CoS-VQ (Coordinated Shared-Scale Vector Quantization), which preserves low-dimensional codewords while jointly optimizing hard indices and their shared scale across positions. The key challenge is scale-induced coupling: the optimal scale depends on the entire codeword combination and, in turn, changes candidate rankings across positions, so pointwise updates can stall even after scale re-optimization. CoS-VQ collects candidates at multiple probe scales and constructs a tangent separable upper bound for the residual-aware quadratic objective. By reducing candidate comparisons to lower envelopes of lines over positive scales, it identifies finitely many representative intervals for joint index--scale updates without exhaustively enumerating codeword combinations. On Qwen3.8-27B, CoS-VQ outperforms QTIP and LLVQ on the evaluated language modeling, coding, and reasoning benchmarks. Ablations from the same initialization further show larger gains from joint updates than from scale-only refinement, highlighting joint selection as an alternative to increasing codeword dimensionality. The code is available at https://github.com/xzktx003/Cos_VQ.

results.title: WAGES: Workload-Aware GPU Sharing System for Energy-Efficient Serverless LLM Serving
results.venue: SC25-W: Workshops of the International Conference for High Performance Computing, Networking, Storage and Analysis
results.abstract: Serverless LLM serving reduces operational costs by elastically provisioning GPUs and charging users only for actual usage. However, existing systems mainly optimize cold-start latency while overlooking two inefficiencies: (i) static, exclusive GPU allocation that over-provisions compute resources, lowering utilization and inflating hardware costs, and (ii) reliance on hardware-controlled clock frequencies, wasting energy. Our measurements show that many LLM workloads can meet SLOs with partial SM allocations and reduced clock speeds, enabling opportunities for GPU multiplexing and dynamic clock scaling to reduce energy consumption.We propose WAGES, a workload-aware GPU-sharing system for energy-efficient serverless LLM serving. WAGES uses NVIDIA MPS to co-locate multiple LLMs on a single GPU, dynamically tuning SM partitions and clock speeds to match workload demands while preserving SLOs. A two-tier scheduling framework coordinates global GPU consolidation and local SLO-aware scheduling with on-the-fly tuning. It also overlaps model/KV migration with execution to reduce reconfiguration overheads. On real-world LLM traces, WAGES improves SLO attainment by up to 4% over state-of-the-art GPU sharing while cutting energy use by up to 26%, showing that fine-grained, workload-aware sharing can improve SLO attainment and reduce energy consumption simultaneously.CCS Concepts• Computing methodologies → Self-organization; Planning and scheduling.

results.title: Reducing Data Transfer Overhead with CXL-Based Near-Data Processing for LLM Inference
results.abstract: In Large Language Models (LLMs), the Key-Value (KV) cache demands a substantial memory footprint as the input sequence length grows. Such memory requirements can exceed the size of model parameters and become unmanageable within limited GPU memory. In this paper, we offload the KV cache to Compute Express Link (CXL) memory and leverage Near-Data Processing (NDP) to select and transfer only the KV cache entries that highly affect model accuracy. Our approach reduces the data transfer overhead caused by limited CXL bandwidth and achieves an average 1.45× speedup over the baseline GPU with CXL memory.
